title: Faster camera-based speed enforcement and processing
subtitle: Also: King-Victoria transit hub, symphony funding referral, development charge complaint, police budget process, church grant request.
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee spent most of its morning on camera-based traffic enforcement. It recommended that staff study speeding up the automated speed enforcement program to 32 sites in 2023 and report on expanding it to all school zones. Staff are also to report by the second quarter on a regional processing centre and third-party providers, hold workshops with township staff on rural traffic calming, and look at community safety zones, including region-wide {{vote:m9}}.

The committee recommended dismissing a development charge complaint about a self-storage site at 375 New Dundee Road {{vote:m1}}. It also recommended authorizing a cost-sharing agreement with Metrolinx and a $450,000 consulting agreement for the King-Victoria Transit Hub {{vote:m5}}.

On funding requests, the committee recommended referring a $100,000 Kitchener-Waterloo Symphony request to the February 22 budget committee {{vote:m6}} and taking no action on a church's request for a grant equal to its development charges {{vote:m7}}. It also recommended asking the police chief to present the draft police budget to Regional Council, area municipalities and the community before the board finalizes it {{vote:m10}}. These are recommendations that Council must still adopt.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended a regional administrative penalties system, a joint request for information, study of 32 speed enforcement sites in 2023, a roadmap for all school zones, a processing centre report, rural workshops and a review of community safety zones {{vote:m9}}.

decisions.item: Development charge complaint, 375 New Dundee Road
decisions.detail: The committee recommended dismissing the complaint seeking a credit for a watermain, in line with staff's view that the charge was properly applied {{vote:m1}}.

The committee recommended authorizing an amended cost-sharing agreement with Metrolinx for Phase 1 and a consulting agreement with WZMH Architects with an upset limit of $450,000 plus taxes {{vote:m5}}.
The committee recommended referring the $100,000 one-time funding request to the Strategic Planning and Budget Committee on February 22, 2023 {{vote:m6}}.
The committee recommended taking no action on the $288,441 grant request for a community centre {{vote:m7}}.
The committee recommended asking the police chief to present the draft budget to Regional Council, area municipalities and the community, with community engagement beforehand {{vote:m10}}.
The committee recommended continuing Regional membership in both associations for this term of Council, subject to annual budget approval.

debate: On cameras, councillors pressed for faster, more ambitious action. One said 32 sites meant moving a few cameras around rather than adding cameras, so the motion was amended to cover adding cameras. Staff said processing capacity is the limit on expansion.

Rural councillors said speeding in towns and villages has gone unaddressed for too long. Staff explained that community safety zones must be designated by the road authority, and that school zones are narrowly defined in the Highway Traffic Act.
On third-party processing, a councillor urged using providers already set up. Staff said providers had told them they were not yet ready, and agreed to report back.

On the symphony, some councillors supported the request but wanted it considered at budget time alongside other requests and the grant policy. Concerns included the lower grant allocation and mixed messages to community groups.

On the police budget, supporters said earlier presentations would give council and the public a chance to comment. Some stressed that engagement should reach groups who find board delegations intimidating. Others cautioned against divisive language and noted police morale and resident concerns about crime.
